text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: production api-gateway (us-west-2) — elevated 5xx (502/504) and timeouts. Alert: 5xx rate spiked to ~6.8% over 1m. Dashboard: https://observability.redwood/api-gw/alerts/4398765432 :rotating_light:

alice-oncall: acked. jumping in. first look at ingress metrics now.

ben-platform: seen this start ~22:02 UTC, correlates with a config rollout to the L7 muxes at 22:00. 95th latency rising, connection errors from edge proxies.

carla-sre: any customer-facing impact confirmed? david-support, what are support tickets showing?

David-support: multiple customers hit timeouts 22:03-22:10. Noted: partner-acme (enterprise) saw ~40% of API calls failing, modal: 502. Open ticket: #INC-5891.

alice-oncall: quick blast radius: apis behind mux-service-a and mux-service-c. internal health checks for backend pools still look OK, so may be mux layer or upstream connection pool exhaustion.

ben-platform: rolling back the mux config is possible but disruptive. Let's try targeted mitigations first: 1) enable short-circuit circuit-breaker on mux-service-a to stop retry storms, 2) reduce client-side retries at the edge to 1, 3) temporarily route a small % to eu-west. Can we flip traffic?

alice-oncall: starting mitigation step 1 now. command: ``kubectl annotate svc/mux-service-a unhealthy-override=true --namespace=ingress`` applying circuit tripping rules.

alice-oncall: logs: ```
[22:04:12] mux-a conn_pool: exhausted, pending=512
[22:04:13] upstream connect error: connection refused
[22:04:14] returning 502 to client
```

carla-sre: good catch. If connection pool exhausted, reducing concurrency and enabling backpressure at the mux is right. Can we drop keep-alive for a bit to free connections?

ben-platform: issuing traffic shift to EU for 10% now: ``trafficctl shift --svc api-gateway --from us-west-2 --to eu-west-1 --pct 10`` watching.

alice-oncall: also toggled edge retry multiplier to 0.5 -> effectively 1 retry. Patch posted: ``envoy-config:update retry_policy: max_retries:1``

incident-bot: Update: 5xx rate down to 3.1% after initial measures (22:06). Latency p95 improving slowly.

David-support: customers reporting fewer failures but partner-acme still seeing issues for some endpoints. Will escalate to account execs.

alice-oncall: doing a deeper trace: errors show upstream connection refusals to pool node 10. Node 10 CPU is spiking (95%). Backend seems overloaded by sudden fanout from mux. Possible regression in mux multiplexing.

carla-sre: can we cordon that backend node or gracefully drain? If it's unhealthy we should remove it from LB.

ben-platform: draining node 10: ``svcctl drain node-10 --grace 30s`` now. Also scaling backend pool by +3 replicas as a safety.

alice-oncall: after node drain and scale: connection refusals dropped, 5xx now ~1.1% (22:12). Edge p50/p95 latency trending down.

erica-pm: thanks — can we confirm customer impact window for postmortem? Start: 22:00, major spike until mitigation at 22:06, residual errors until 22:12. I'll capture impacted customers list.

David-support: updated INC-5891 with timeline + customers: partner-acme, beta-shop, mobile-proxy.

carla-sre: recommend follow-ups: 1) revert the recent mux rollout and re-run canary with lowered concurrency, 2) add connection pool autoscaling or better backpressure controls, 3) run chaos test for connection pool exhaustion.

alice-oncall: agreed. I'll open a rollback RFC and schedule a canary with stricter limits. Also will capture heap/cpu dumps from the mux pods for RCA.

incident-bot: Paging update: on-call handoff in 30m, alice-oncall to hand off to carla-sre at 23:00 UTC.

alice-oncall: handing off now. brief: root likely mux pooling bug triggered by recent config rollout 22:00. Mitigations applied: circuit-breaker, reduced retries, traffic shift 10% to eu-west, drained node-10, scaled backend +3. Current status: degraded -> stabilizing. Logs/commands saved in incident runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/incidents/4398765432

carla-sre: taking over. I'll keep watch for 2h and coordinate rollback if we see regression.

erica-pm: notifying sales + CS. tagging postmortem owners: @alice-oncall (RCA author), @ben-platform (mitigations & infra change), @carla-sre (follow-up ops).

alice-oncall: thanks — will post a short blameless timeline and root cause hypothesis by EOD. 

carla-sre: adding automated alert: if 5xx > 2% for 5m after rollback flag, auto-circuit and page.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. No active page. End of thread.
